data.name: Ashishay
data.gender_notes: Ashishay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashishay is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘ashisha’ and ‘ay’, which together mean ‘wish, desire, or happiness’. This name is a reflection of the deep longing and hope that is inherent in every human heart for joy, peace, and fulfillment. The name Ashishay carries the meaning “Wish, Desire, Happiness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ashishay usually hope their child will grow to embody wish, desire, happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your life be filled with deep desires and the strength to fulfill them.
data.etymology: Ashishay belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wish, Desire, Happiness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashishay total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: अशिषाय
in_sanskrit.meaning: Not to be longed for, not to be desired
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: अशिष् - Not to be, ईषा - Longing, आय - Desired. A name for a boy who is not longed for or desired, or for someone who does not desire anything.

in_hindi.name: अशिषाय
in_hindi.long_meaning: अशिषा - अपमाननीय (shameful, disgraceful), ईषा - ईषा (desire), आय - आय (towards). A name for a boy who is not desirable, or for someone who does not have a desire or is ashamed of something.

in_tamil.name: அசிஷய
in_tamil.long_meaning: அசிஷ் - அவர்கள் (They), ஷி - ஷ (Not), யாவன் - வான் (Man). A name for a boy who is not desired by others.

in_telugu.name: అశిషేయ
in_telugu.long_meaning: అశిష్ - అదేశ్ (not desirable), శేయ - శేశ్ (desirable), యదేశ్ (beloved). A name for a boy who is not desirable or for someone who is not beloved.

The pursuit of happiness and joy is a fundamental aspect of Hinduism, and is seen as an essential means of leading a meaningful and purposeful life. Ashishay is a reminder of this eternal human quest and serves as a constant inspiration to strive towards achieving our heart's desires and living a life filled with happiness and contentment.

This Self, known as the Atman or the soul, is seen as the source of all happiness and fulfillment, and the ultimate destination of all human endeavors. Ashishay serves as a powerful reminder of this eternal truth and inspires us to strive towards realizing the inner happiness and peace that comes from connecting with our true Self. historical_references.reference: Ashishay is mentioned in the 14th century Indian epic poem Mahabharata as the name of a powerful weapon gifted by Lord Shiva to Arjuna.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It narrates the story of the Kurukshetra war between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.

historical_references.reference: Ashishay is also mentioned in the 16th century Indian text, the Purana Samhita, as a powerful celestial weapon that was used by Lord Indra to defeat the demon Tripura.
